policies.description: Any update_change request must include the mandatory field `change_id`.
references: Mandatory Fields: Any request to create or update a record must validate all mandatory fields.

policies.description: When the `status` parameter is provided in an `update_change` request, its value must be one of the permitted statuses: new, assess, authorize, scheduled, implement, review, closed, or canceled.
If the calling user’s role does not grant authority for the requested update_change operation, the system must return a 403 Forbidden error.
references: 403 Forbidden: Permission denied (user role lacks authority for the operation).

policies.description: The update_change call must be performed as a single validated operation; no additional actions may be combined with it.
references: Atomic Operations: Perform one validated operation at a time, except when using approved batch endpoints.

policies.description: When using the `update_change` tool, check the caller’s confirmed role (available from the authenticated user record). If the caller’s role is **Manager** or **Administrator**, the payload may contain any allowed `status` value (`new`, `assess`, `authorize`, `scheduled`, `implement`, `review`, `closed`, `canceled`). If the caller’s role is any other role (e.g., Agent, Reporter), the payload must either omit the `status` field or set it explicitly to `new`. Any payload that attempts to change `status` to a value other than `new` for a non‑Manager/Administrator must be rejected before invoking the API.
references: | Agent (agent) | Cannot bypass approvals, or change system administration settings. |

policies.description: If the caller’s authenticated role is **Agent**, an `update_change` call may include any updatable fields **except** the `status` field, which must either be omitted or set to the value `new`. Any payload that tries to set `status` to any value other than `new` (e.g., `assess`, `authorize`, `scheduled`, `implement`, `review`, `closed`, `canceled`) must be blocked before the tool is invoked.
references: | Agent (agent) | Cannot bypass approvals, or change system administration settings. |

archive.description: When `assigned_to` is provided, the referenced user must have `users.active = true`.
references: User Status: Ensure any user being assigned to (assigned_to) or updated is users.active = true.
archive.comments:
The policy directly applies to the `update_change` tool because that tool accepts an optional `assigned_to` field. Before calling the tool we can verify the target user’s active flag by using a user‑lookup tool (e.g., `get_user` or `list_users`). This makes the policy enforceable and verifiable prior to execution. While the rule is not exclusive to the change‑update operation (it could also apply to incident creation, assignment, etc.), it is still relevant to the target tool. The description is clear and complete, requiring no external context. Score: 4 – the policy is clear, enforceable, and relevant, with a minor deduction for being generic rather than tool‑specific.
